newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy PM hails bank deal, consumer group complains.
newsitem.headline: Italy PM hails bank deal, consumer group complains.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi hailed a successful bid by insurer INA and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro to take control of Banco di Napoli, but a leading consumer group branded the winning offer "offensive".

The government announced on Saturday it had accepted a joint bid by recently privatised INA and Treasury-controlled BNL to pay 61.6 billion lire ($39 million) for a 60 percent stake in southern Italy's largest bank.
The sale, which is due to be finalised in March, will create one of the largest banking groups in Italy with 1,400 branches, deposits worth 143.2 trillion lire and loans of 153.2 trillion.
"The agreement between Banco di Napoli, BNL and INA is a winning card in the restructuring of the Italian banking sector," a satisfied Prodi told reporters.

However the national association for the defence of bank users (ADUSBEF) said the government would have done better putting loss-making Banco di Napoli into liquidation and said it would challenge the sale in the courts.

The Italian Treasury last year sunk some 2.2 trillion lire of fresh funds into Banco di Napoli to keep the loss-making group afloat. In addition it set up a so-called bad bank to take on some 12.36 trillion lire of the group's non-performing loans.
Banco di Napoli was put on the market at the end of last year and banking sources said the government had been hoping to persuade the buyer to pay a higher price.
In the event only INA/BNL and state controlled Mediocredito Centrale placed an offer, with the latter bid being ruled inadmissable because it sought to change the sale conditions.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told reporters on Saturday the low price reflected the problems of the southern economy and the consequent credit risk for firms trading there.
ADUSBEF said Ciampi should have rejected the final offer.

"It would have been much more serious and honest that, following the offensive offers of INA/BNL and Mediocredito, the (government) had started to put Banco di Napoli into liquidation," the group said in a statement.
"It is the only possible road to truly saving Banco di Napoli's assets and to force into the open those responsible for the (bank's poor) management," it added.

Banco di Napoli is believed to have lost a staggering six trillion lire over the past three years, the highest in Italian banking history, with a mix of adverse economic conditions and poor leadership bringing the long-established bank to its knees.
Newspapers reported that the INA-BNL consortium would inject between 900 billion and 1.2 trillion lire into Banco di Napoli.

INA said last month that if its bid for Banco di Napoli was successful it would take 51 percent of the firm and BNL 49 percent. Ciampi said on Saturday he could not rule out an eventual fusion of BNL and Banco di Napoli.
BNL, which itself has only recently emerged from a government bail-out, said in a statement on Sunday it hoped for a "strong and swift intergration with Banco di Napoli".
INA said it would now launch a thorough investigation into the situation at Banco di Napoli.

"This will provide us with an industrial plan for the relaunch of Banco di Napoli which remains an indispensable motor for the economic and business activity of the South," it said in a statement. $1 = 1,570 lire
